_comment: WARROOM-SYNTHETIC-001 declarative scenario table (card §🟢). One row per scenario: name, injection, expected tile state, expected alert, teardown. Executed by test/warroom-synthetic-suite.test.mjs, which looks up the handler for `id` — adding scenario 8 is a new row here plus one new handler function, never a refactor of the runner.

scenarios.name: Killed cron, three-stage progression
scenarios.injection: Stop writing run rows for a staging job of known cadence; evaluate at age<1.5x, 1.5x<=age<=3x, age>3x cadence
scenarios.expected_alert: BLOCKED — GATE-A unresolved (see report): production R1 is a fleet-wide config_gap placeholder, not a per-job late/stale rule. Render half asserted in full; alert half asserted against REAL current R1 behavior (fires config_gap, not per-job).

scenarios.name: Non-zero exit (Tech Intel)
scenarios.injection: Synthetic run_log row: job=tech-intel, exit_code=1, error set

scenarios.name: Stalled run / STUCK
scenarios.injection: Synthetic run_log row: started_at set, finished_at null, age > 2x p95

scenarios.name: Cross-source agreement (OPS/DATA/QUEUE, state-endpoint level)
scenarios.injection: Same run_state() result fed through the one shared join (warroom-ops-join.js) consumed by both /api/ops/timeline and /api/ops/cron-today
scenarios.expected_tile_state: identical run_id + state string across both call sites for the same job/slot
scenarios.expected_alert: n/a (structural agreement check, not an alert scenario)

scenarios.name: Stale feed propagation
scenarios.injection: Staging feed file aged past cadence x2 (fs.utimesSync on a file under a temp staging root, never the real finance-data.json)

scenarios.name: Unrenderable payload (5x)
scenarios.injection: 5 payloads matching the observed [object Object] shape passed to WarroomRender.formatTelemetryEvent
scenarios.expected_alert: BLOCKED — counter exists (WarroomRender.counters.unrenderable_event) but is not yet consumed by any alert-engine.js rule (confirmed by code inspection, not fabricated). Counter-increment half asserted in full.

scenarios.name: Clock skew
scenarios.injection: Event timestamped in the future relative to `now`
scenarios.expected_tile_state: ERROR — clock skew, no numeric/time value rendered, sort order uncorrupted
scenarios.expected_alert: BLOCKED — no §2.2 rule named for clock-skew events specifically (confirmed by code inspection of alert-engine.js's R1-R6 + stuck watchdog)

scenarios.name: Single source per number (cache_hit_rate)
scenarios.injection: cache_hit_rate changed by a known delta in the canonical view input
scenarios.expected_tile_state: every tile reading that figure moves by exactly the delta in the same evaluation
scenarios.expected_alert: n/a (runtime single-source check, not an alert scenario)
